A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CRAFT research work. Their text, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated from v1's appendices into v2's main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original NQ-Tables retrieval and answer-generation results, query-perturbation experiments, stage ablations, few-shot evaluations and token-count measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original NQ-Tables experiments and reports additional OTT-QA evaluations, model configurations, context comparisons and qualitative failure cases.

M1.justification: The training-free three-stage architecture remains. v2 Section 3 introduces dataset-specific component substitutions: Jina Embeddings v3 for OTT-QA row ranking and dense retrieval, and gemini-embedding-001 for final reranking. It also adds a text-embedding-3-large variant for NQ-Tables. These adapt the existing pipeline without introducing a new training objective or retrieval architecture.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only NQ-Tables. v2 adds retrieval over OTT-QA's 419,183-table corpus and answer generation on its table-and-passage questions. This substantially extends coverage to a hybrid multi-hop benchmark, although the answer-generation evaluation supplies gold passages.

E2.justification: The main NQ retrieval comparison adds Re2G and released DTR(M)+HN and DTR(S)+HN checkpoints in v2 Table 2. Those DTR variants previously appeared only in v1's perturbation comparison. v2 Figure 2 also includes DTR variants in downstream QA comparisons. The established comparator set is otherwise largely retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an oracle OTT-QA protocol pairing retrieved tables with gold passages, a gold-table-plus-passage control, full-table versus mini-table QA configurations, and additional model evaluations including GPT-4o. These substantially expand the evaluation design. Figure 1 also changes the intermediate shortlist label from 1,000 to 100; because v1 already evaluated 100-candidate reranking, this does not establish an actual change to the earlier runs.

E4.justification: v1 already contains stage, paraphrase, few-shot and token-count analyses. v2 adds full-table versus mini-table F1/context-length comparisons on NQ-Tables and OTT-QA (Figures 2, 6 and 7), plus two failure case studies (Tables 16–17). These investigate whether context filtering prevents missed answers and incorrect answer extraction, extending the earlier analysis beyond token savings.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The new curves continue point-estimate reporting. Average recall changes in the perturbation tables are not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds OTT-QA results and GPT-4o F1 scores of 56.76 and 67.72 at n=1 and n=5. Its new large-reranker NQ results are 49.84/86.83/97.17 at R@1/10/50; the original small-reranker results remain. Existing entries also change: Qwen's n=1 zero-shot F1 goes from 33.33 to 39.73, THYME's n=5 Mistral F1 from 39.29 to 37.20, and SPLADE's without-description R@1 from 32.64 to 31.06. These comprise new configurations and revised results, not uniformly established same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems, proofs or a mathematical framework. v2 adds informal computational accounting and model-choice explanations, without introducing substantive formal definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims state-of-the-art NQ R@1, whereas v1 emphasizes competitive retrieval and acknowledges lower R@1. It extends headline performance claims to competitive zero-shot OTT-QA retrieval and adds up to 33-fold fewer online embedding calls as an explicit contribution. These broaden the claimed scope and computational benefits.

C2.justification: v1 explains SPLADE's unchanged description-ablation scores through context saturation; v2 reports a benefit and removes that explanation. v2 also adds interpretations concerning contextual noise, ambiguous entities and retrieval-versus-answerability failures, alongside offline/online computation trade-offs. Its limitations explicitly distinguish oracle-passage evaluation from full open retrieval and identify unaddressed multi-hop retrieval and multimodal tables.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project link advertised for code and data, and documents precomputed row embeddings, sparse indexing, ANN search and on-demand mini-table encoding in Section 4.4. Table 2 and Appendix A clarify checkpoint provenance. The baseline hyperparameter table and three prompt templates already existed in v1; the newly documented execution details do not establish that the earlier implementation changed.

R1.justification: v2's introduction adds discussion of earlier cascaded systems, including Wang et al. (2011), Hu et al. (2019) and Re2G, positioning CRAFT against trained retrieval pipelines. References supporting OTT-QA and the additional embedding models also appear. This expands context while retaining the central positioning around modular, training-free table retrieval.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative into dedicated benchmark, numbered results, computational-efficiency and ablation sections. Much of v1 Appendix A moves into the main text, and the remaining appendices are redistributed. The abstract, contribution list, conclusion and limitations receive substantial rewriting, beyond the insertion of new experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds three context-length performance figures, OTT-QA result tables and two case-study tables. It expands the dataset-statistics and stage-wise tables and relocates existing token-count and ablation displays into the main text. Figure 1's shortlist annotations and table emphasis conventions change. The original prompt figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence by addressing v1's explicitly acknowledged single-benchmark limitation and testing full-table versus mini-table answer quality beyond token savings. Failure cases and explicit oracle-setting limitations improve interpretation. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses: OTT-QA Stage 2 R@10 conflicts between Tables 3 and 8 (81.88 versus 87.35), and the 33-fold online-call claim does not clearly separate baseline precomputation from inference. Those issues limit specific conclusions but do not erase the substantial gains in validation and diagnostic evidence.
